periods.analysis: At 15% complete and green, Neighborhood Library Modernization is off to a steady start, with the benefits already visible to families, seniors, and students who use our branches every week. The Eastside branch renovation is complete 150 days early, giving that neighborhood brighter study rooms, safer circulation, and more flexible community meeting space ahead of the school-year rush. Self-checkout kiosks are complete across all branches 30 days early, and early floor observations from the Main, Eastside, and Harbor Point teams show shorter waits at peak after-school and lunch-hour periods. Riverside branch renovation is in progress with 75 days to its milestone, and the project team is sequencing interior work so the branch can keep limited holds pickup and children’s programming available as long as safely possible.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green trajectory by assigning a weekly owner walk-through at Riverside with Facilities, Library Operations, and the contractor to protect the 75-day milestone window. Extend the Eastside lessons learned by documenting the furniture, lighting, and service-desk layout choices that residents are responding to positively, then use that checklist for Riverside. Keep kiosk ambassadors in lobbies for another full month so residents who are less comfortable with technology experience the upgrade as welcoming, not transactional.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 15% to 20%, a 5-point quarter-over-quarter increase, and the initiative remains green because the completed assets are holding up under real resident use. Eastside, complete 150 days early, has become our proof point: weekend room bookings and story-time attendance are giving staff practical feedback on how renovated spaces support community life. The all-branch self-checkout rollout, complete 30 days early, is now moving from installation to adoption, with branch managers tracking when staff time is freed up for reader advisory, account help, and youth services. Riverside remains in progress with 75 days to its milestone, and the winter construction calendar is the main operational item we are managing carefully.
periods.recommendations: Continue the weekly Riverside construction huddle and add a weather-and-delivery risk log for flooring, millwork, and electrical fixtures so winter delays are surfaced early. Sustain resident adoption of the kiosks by keeping one clearly identified staff helper near the front-of-house zone during the first two hours after school. Use Eastside’s first full quarter of operations to set practical service standards for renovated branches, including room reset time, signage placement, and quiet-zone monitoring.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 20% to 25%, another 5-point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green with the modernization work now settling into a dependable rhythm. Eastside’s renovation, complete 150 days early, is no longer just a capital milestone; it is giving residents a warmer, more usable civic living room during the colder months. Self-checkout kiosks remain complete across all branches 30 days early, and circulation staff are using the reduced transaction load to spend more time with job seekers, caregivers, and students who need one-on-one help. Riverside is still in progress with 75 days to its milestone, and the team is coordinating noisy work outside tutoring blocks and senior computer classes.
periods.recommendations: Hold the pace by confirming Riverside’s next 30-day lookahead schedule with specific quiet-hour protections for tutoring, tax-help appointments, and morning senior use. Extend the kiosk success by refreshing signage in the five busiest branches with plain-language instructions and multilingual prompts. Begin a resident feedback pulse at Eastside and Riverside so design decisions are tied to how people actually feel using the buildings, not only to construction completion.

periods.analysis: Progress increased from 25% to 30%, a steady 5-point quarter-over-quarter movement, and the initiative continues in green status. Eastside remains a strong early win, complete 150 days early and now helping us understand how modernized branches can support longer visits, group learning, and neighborhood meetings. The self-checkout kiosks, complete 30 days early across all branches, are becoming part of normal service rather than a new technology project, which is exactly the resident-centered outcome we wanted. Riverside remains in progress with 75 days to its milestone, and summer reading traffic makes careful phasing especially important so construction does not crowd out children’s programming.
periods.recommendations: Sustain green performance by placing a dedicated summer-reading circulation plan at Riverside, including temporary wayfinding, stroller clearance, and a protected children’s program path. Extend the modernization benefits by using kiosk transaction data to redeploy staff hours toward summer learning sign-ups and digital literacy coaching. Keep the Riverside contractor on a two-week constraint review focused on deliveries, inspections, and any work that affects public access during peak youth programming.

periods.analysis: The initiative moved from 30% to 35%, maintaining the same 5-point quarter-over-quarter gain and staying green as we enter the heavier community-use season. Eastside, complete 150 days early, continues to show the value of finishing well: residents are using the flexible rooms for homework clubs, neighborhood association meetings, and small business workshops. Self-checkout kiosks remain complete at all branches 30 days early, and staff are increasingly treating them as one access option among many, preserving a welcoming human service model. Riverside is in progress with 75 days to its milestone, and back-to-school demand is the operational context shaping our phasing choices.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the current pace by aligning Riverside construction access routes with school-year peak hours, especially the 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. student window. Extend Eastside’s community-room practices to other branches by creating a simple playbook for furniture presets, after-hours handoff, and youth program storage. Continue kiosk support with targeted refresh training for substitutes and part-time staff so service quality stays consistent branch to branch.

periods.analysis: Progress rose from 35% to 40%, another 5-point quarter-over-quarter improvement, and the initiative remains green because the work is both on track and meaningful to residents. Eastside’s renovation, complete 150 days early, has given us a full seasonal cycle of operating experience, from summer reading to fall civic meetings. The self-checkout kiosks, complete across all branches 30 days early, are now a stable service layer, helping staff handle holiday and school-break surges without making residents feel rushed. Riverside remains in progress with 75 days to its milestone, and the team is watching year-end procurement, inspection scheduling, and contractor availability closely.
periods.recommendations: Protect the green status by locking Riverside inspection dates early and confirming backup vendor availability for any long-lead finish items. Sustain kiosk performance through a year-end maintenance sweep, including receipt printers, barcode scanners, accessibility height checks, and screen-language settings at every branch. Use Eastside’s first-year operating data to refine the next modernization package before design assumptions become costly change orders.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 40% to 45%, a continued 5-point quarter-over-quarter increase, and remains green with a clear line of sight to the halfway mark. Eastside, complete 150 days early, continues to anchor the resident story: modern libraries are not just nicer buildings, they are places where people can learn, connect, and get help without friction. The all-branch kiosk milestone remains complete 30 days early, and staff are now focusing on equity of use, making sure older adults, English learners, and residents with disabilities can choose self-service without losing personal support. Riverside remains in progress with 75 days to its milestone, with first-quarter weather and utility coordination being managed through tighter daily site communication.
periods.recommendations: Keep momentum by requiring a daily Riverside field note during weather-sensitive work, with issues escalated the same day to Facilities and Library Operations. Extend the resident-centered kiosk model by pairing accessibility checks with short staff scripts that offer help without pressure. Begin preparing the communications plan for the 50% initiative mark so residents can see what has been completed, what is underway, and how modernization is improving everyday library visits.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 45% to 50%, a 5-point quarter-over-quarter gain, and the initiative reaches the halfway point in green status. That is a meaningful milestone for Harborview residents: Eastside is complete 150 days early, kiosks are complete across all branches 30 days early, and Riverside remains in progress with 75 days to its milestone rather than drifting into uncertainty. The work now feels less like a set of projects and more like a service transformation, with faster routine transactions, more flexible public space, and staff time increasingly available for the people who need guidance. Our next risk is not momentum but consistency, making sure every branch experience reflects the same warmth and access that residents are seeing in the completed work.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by conducting a midpoint readiness review covering Riverside schedule, branch operating impacts, kiosk reliability, and resident feedback trends. Extend the modernization model by selecting the next two branch areas for design scoping using Eastside outcomes, Riverside constraints, and service-demand data. Publish a simple resident-facing midpoint update that explains the 50% completion mark, celebrates completed milestones, and invites practical feedback before the next phase is locked.

periods.analysis: 80% complete. 0 of 3 milestones are done. Next up: Eastside branch renovation (due Feb 26, 2026).
periods.recommendations: Review the late milestones with the project owner and confirm recovery dates before the next reporting cycle.
